classification_formulations.name: A. healthy vs damaged
classification_formulations.difficulty: Moderate but damage class is heterogeneous and imbalanced.
classification_formulations.leakage_risk: High if windows or bearing IDs cross partitions; low only with bearing-disjoint evaluation.
classification_formulations.suitability: Acceptable detection baseline, but less diagnostic depth.

classification_formulations.name: B. healthy vs artificial vs real
classification_formulations.meaning: Separates undamaged state and damage provenance.
classification_formulations.difficulty: Likely easy in part because machining versus lifetime-test morphology differs.
classification_formulations.leakage_risk: Bearing leakage plus a provenance shortcut; class is not a pure physical fault type.
classification_formulations.suitability: Useful domain-shift analysis, not primary industrial diagnosis.

classification_formulations.name: C. healthy vs real outer-ring vs real inner-ring
classification_formulations.meaning: Bearing condition and physically meaningful damage-location classification using real lifetime-test damage only.
classification_formulations.difficulty: Meaningful: inner-ring signatures are modulated and real damage is heterogeneous.
classification_formulations.leakage_risk: Manageable only by bearing-disjoint partitions; exclude the 3 combined-location bearings from these pure labels.
classification_formulations.suitability: Strong: three clear classes, 16 independent IDs, and direct temporal/frequency relevance.

classification_formulations.name: D. real damage-type classification
classification_formulations.meaning: Separates official main modes (fatigue/pitting from plastic-deformation/indentations).
classification_formulations.difficulty: High but plastic deformation has only 3 IDs and locations are mixed.
classification_formulations.leakage_risk: Bearing leakage plus location as a confound.
classification_formulations.suitability: Insufficiently balanced for robust train/validation/test bearing splits.
classification_formulations.recommendation: Not primary; possible descriptive analysis only.

classification_formulations.name: E. operating-condition classification

independent_bearings_per_class.each_condition: 32 bearings if every archive has all four settings

classification_formulations.meaning: Classifies test-rig setting, not bearing condition.
classification_formulations.leakage_risk: Very high if condition labels correlate with windows from the same recordings; not a bearing-damage task.
classification_formulations.suitability: Useful as a nuisance/generalization factor, not the Track 1 target.
classification_formulations.recommendation: Use as held-out robustness analysis only, not primary.

recommended_task.task: Three-class, bearing-disjoint classification of vibration segments: healthy vs real outer-ring damage vs real inner-ring damage.
recommended_task.why: It uses actual lifetime-test damage, avoids classifying machining provenance, preserves clear physical labels, has 5/5 damaged IDs plus 6 healthy IDs, and directly tests whether temporal transients plus frequency signatures improve location-sensitive classification.
recommended_task.grouping_requirement: All files and all windows for a bearing ID must stay in exactly one partition. With 6/5/5 IDs, a stratified 3/1/1 per-class split is possible for the five-ID classes; the exact fixed split must still be approved/declared before creation.
recommended_task.input_rationale: Vibration is the established bearing-diagnosis signal; the official paper reports stronger vibration classification than motor-current classification. A single vibration channel also keeps the proposed temporal/frequency fusion focused on Track 1 rather than conflating it with multimodal sensor fusion. Motor current should be retained for a future, separately declared robustness/low-cost-sensing experiment.
recommended_task.metric_status: Recommendation only. The supplied hackathon DOCX does not prescribe a Track 1 primary metric; it must not be treated as organizer-mandated until confirmed.
